root_causes.root_cause: _inject_arabic_structural_headings (RFC-027 D4, converters.py:85-115) has two bugs causing Arabic structural markers to not be promoted to ATX headings: (1) prev_blank guard requires a blank line before each marker but OCR output from scanned Arabic PDFs flows continuously without blank-line separators, so only the first article gets promoted; (2) len(t)<=60 char limit is too tight for Arabic legal headings that include article titles (common lines are 66-76+ chars). Both bugs compound to produce flat/depth-0/depth-1 trees for Arabic legal docs despite clean text extraction.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/converters.py::_inject_arabic_structural_headings -> md_to_tree (flat tree) -> validate_tree (depth<2) -> flat success path (cat_b_promoted)
root_causes.suggested_fix: (1) Remove or relax the prev_blank guard: instead of requiring the prior line to be blank, check whether the line STARTS with an Arabic structural marker regardless of prior context (the len<=60/80 guard already filters mid-paragraph references). (2) Raise the char limit from 60 to at least 100 to accommodate Arabic article headings with titles. Both changes are in _inject_arabic_structural_headings, ~5-10 lines changed.

root_causes.root_cause: _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE in helpers.py (line 1539-1554) has no pattern for standalone Roman numeral clause markers (I., II., III., IV. etc.). It only matches 'Part [IVX]+' as a compound marker but not bare Roman numeral sub-clause numbering. The Haftpflicht-Besondere-Bedingungen doc uses Roman-numeral sub-levels (I through XXVII) as its 27-clause sub-structure, which the ordinal splitter cannot detect, leaving the tree at depth-2 when it should be depth-3+.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add a standalone Roman-numeral alternative to _OVERSIZED_ORDINAL_RE: r'|(?P<roman>[IVX]+)\.\s' matching patterns like 'I. ', 'II. ', 'III. ' etc. Add corresponding _ordinal_value handling to parse the Roman numeral via _roman_to_int. ~15 lines.

root_causes.root_cause: GHV-TKV-Tarif.pdf has 3 rate tables (horse/dog/cat) collapsed into unsegmented leaf blobs with leaf_concentration=0.39. Table rows are inherently not heading-like markers, so neither md_to_tree (which only splits on ATX headings) nor split_oversized_leaf_nodes (which only splits on ordinal/paragraph markers) can segment them. This is an architectural gap: there is no table-row-as-structural-marker detection. RFC-027 D5 proposed raising the small_doc_promoted threshold but that only changes the verdict, not the structure.
root_causes.code_path: md_to_tree (no headings in table content) -> split_oversized_leaf_nodes (no ordinal markers in table rows)
root_causes.suggested_fix: Add table-aware splitting to split_oversized_leaf_nodes: detect markdown pipe-table boundaries (lines matching |...|...|) and split oversized leaves at table-boundary transitions. Alternatively, in the converter, inject synthetic heading markers between distinct tables (e.g. when a blank line separates two table blocks). ~40-60 lines.
